findings.issue: The plan creates one separate `discountAutomaticBasicCreate` per tier (e.g. three automatic discounts for a 3-tier bundle). Shopify automatic discounts apply to every qualifying cart independently — they have no awareness of each other. When a customer buys 4 items and all three tier thresholds (2, 3, 4 items) are met simultaneously, all three automatic discounts fire and stack, producing a deeply over-discounted order. The plan declares no mutual-exclusion mechanism (e.g. a minimum-quantity exclusive condition, a single discount with dynamic tiers, or a discount code strategy) to ensure only the highest applicable tier applies.
findings.fix: Replace the one-discount-per-tier model with a single automatic discount per bundle whose value is computed dynamically (e.g. via a Shopify Functions discount function that reads item count and selects the correct tier), or document exactly how each tier discount is constrained so lower tiers do not fire when a higher tier qualifies — and resolve the concrete op(s) this requires.

findings.issue: The dataFlow states the attribution handler "inspects discount_applications to find any discount external id matching a known tier", and `bundle_tiers` stores `discount_external_id` as the join key. However, the `orders/paid` webhook payload's `discount_applications` array contains `title`, `type`, `value`, and `value_type` — it does NOT contain the automatic discount's admin API node ID. There is no payload field the coding agent can match against `discount_external_id`, making the documented attribution join unbuildable as written.
findings.fix: Change the attribution strategy to match on discount title: store a deterministic, unique title on each `bundle_tiers` row (add a `discount_title` text column), set that exact title when calling `discountAutomaticBasicCreate`/`discountAutomaticBxgyCreate`, and update `attribute-bundle-purchase` dataNeeds and `payloadBinding` to reflect that the join key is `discount_applications[].title`, not a node ID.

findings.issue: Even if attribution is corrected to match by title, the `bundle_tiers` table has no column storing the discount title used when creating the Shopify discount. Without a stored title, the coding agent has no join key: it cannot query `bundle_tiers` by the title it reads from `discount_applications`, and it cannot guarantee the title it later creates in Shopify matches anything queryable locally. The `label` column is described as a human-readable display label, which is merchant-editable and not guaranteed unique across bundles and tiers.
findings.fix: Add a `discount_title` column (role: text, nullable: false) to `bundle_tiers` with the purpose "system-generated unique title written to Shopify at discount creation time and used as the attribution join key"; add a query pattern "single tier looked up by discount title for order attribution matching".

findings.issue: The step declares `op: "product"` (singular) with `consumes: "product external id per component"`. A bundle can have many components; fetching variant availability one product at a time is an N+1 storefront query pattern. The Storefront API exposes `nodes` for batch-fetching multiple products by ID in a single call, but the plan resolves only a single-product op, giving the coding agent no instruction to batch. For a 10-component bundle this is 10 sequential API calls on every widget page load.
findings.fix: Replace the single `product` step with a `nodes` query step that consumes a list of component product external ids and returns variant titles, prices, and availability for all components in one round-trip; update `produces` accordingly.

findings.issue: The capability declares `returnsList: false`, but the corresponding `/widget/bundle` GET contract's `responseShape` includes `component_variants: list`, `next_cursor: text`, and `total_count: count`, signalling a paginated list response. The coding agent receives contradictory signals: the capability says "not a list" while the contract says "paginated list of component variants". This will cause inconsistent handling of the pagination cursor.
findings.fix: Set `returnsList: true` on `fetch-bundle-for-widget` to match the paginated responseShape, and add a note in the capability description that the list is the component variants sub-collection, not multiple bundles.
